title: Decorative-Step Detector for Chain-of-Thought ('Fake Aha Moments')

original_idea.body: Decorative-Step Detector for CoT. Problem: no simple step-ablation tool labels each CoT step as causal or ornamental for open models. Direction: segment CoT into steps, delete/replace each and measure answer change; steps whose removal doesn't change the answer are decorative; report per-model decorative-step statistics.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: step-level causal/decorative labeling directly informs trust in CoT monitoring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Step segmentation + ablation regeneration; clear inherited methodology.

low_compute.reasoning: Per-step ablation multiplies inference; single GPU but non-trivial.

novelty.reasoning: Step-ablation faithfulness exists; turnkey detector may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Step ablation and true-vs-decorative labeling exist; a reusable detector tool is plausibly open.
